einzeiler: Wie verändern historische Ernährungspyramiden und der Fokus auf lebendige Lebensmittel…
kurzfassung: Monica Corrado analysiert im Podcast die Entwicklung der offiziellen US-Ernährungsempfehlungen seit 1992 und kritisiert deren hohen Anteil an Kohlenhydraten und Zucker. Als Gegenmodell stellt sie das Konzept "tot versus lebendig" vor, bei dem rohe, fermentierte und naturbelassene Lebensmittel im Vordergrund stehen. Zudem beantwortet sie Fragen aus dem Chat zu Themen wie Rohmilch, gesunden Fetten und Ballaststoffen.
stichpunkte: Kritik an der Ernährungspyramide von 1992 für ihren hohen Kohlenhydrat- und Zuckeranteil
Darstellung der Entwicklung von Pyramiden und Tellern hin zu den Richtlinien für 2025
Einführung des Konzepts "tot versus lebendig" zur Bewertung der eigenen Ernährung
Definition von totem Essen: verpackt, konserviert, gekocht, pasteurisiert und mikrowelliert
Definition von lebendem Essen: roh, gekeimt, kulturiert und laktofermentiert
Empfehlung für gesunde Fette und den regelmäßigen Verzehr von rohen Tierprodukten
Erklärung von Fermentationsprozessen und der schrittweisen Gewöhnung des Darms an Probiotika
Ablehnung von hochraffinierten Lebensmittelfraktionen wie MCT-Öl zugunsten von Vollwertprodukten

kapitel.titel: The Core Concept: Dead Versus Alive Food
Q&A Session on Dairy, Fats, and Fermentation

clips.hook: The bottom of the pyramid that threw Americans into obesity
clips.text: The host blames the official dietary guidelines introduced in 1992 for rising rates of obesity and diabetes in the United States.

clips.hook: You have permission and an invitation to have more fat in your diet
clips.text: Listeners are advised to gradually increase their daily fat intake up to eight tablespoons, noting that a low-fat diet trend began in the country in 1983.

clips.hook: How much of your food came out of a box? If it's in a box, it's dead
clips.text: Any packaged food sold in a box is categorized as dead sustenance that can remain on shelves indefinitely.

clips.hook: All cooked food is dead, no matter what it is
clips.text: The speaker defines all cooked meals, whether prepared on a stove or in a microwave, as dead nourishment.

clips.hook: Whenever you hear the word highly refined, you should shun it entirely
clips.text: Highly processed items like medium-chain triglyceride oil derived from coconuts should be avoided because the human body rejects refined ingredients.

beschreibung:
Monica Corrado opens this week’s In the Kitchen with Monica livestream with a look at what makes a nourishing plate. Building on previous conversations about real food and nourishment, she reviews changing dietary guidelines before sharing her own framework for thinking about the foods we eat.

Highlights include:
-A look back at food pyramids and dietary guidelines and how recommendations around grains, fats, protein, fruits, and vegetables have changed over time
-Monica’s perspective on traditional fats, animal foods, whole milk, cultured dairy, and properly prepared grains
-The distinction she draws between “dead” foods that are cooked, canned, packaged, or highly processed and “live” foods that are raw, cultured, sprouted, or fermented
-Ideas for incorporating raw and cultured dairy, lacto-fermented foods, sprouted foods, and other traditionally prepared foods into meals
-A Q&A covering fermented foods, cultured dairy, oats, MCT oil, fiber, cooking fats, and more

Monica closes by encouraging viewers to look beyond conventional food pyramids and plates and instead consider how much fresh, raw, cultured, sprouted, or fermented food they are including in their meals—starting with one doable change at a time.
